scope: Full-frame semantic topology audit of the held-out MiniMax-H3 inspect-flower baseline
summary: The new fail-closed topology review rejects the previously selected H3 candidate because its robot body ceases to be one coherent anatomical chain.
evidence: All 124 decoded frames are bound to the candidate SHA-256 and covered by explicit semantic labels.
Only 24/124 frames pass; 100 frames fail unique shoulder attachment and stable-proportion gates.
Eighty-two frames additionally fail the single head-to-torso chain gate.
The annotated 832x480x124 review video has SHA-256 f23f3bc50bd1b3980c9ac42b0cc5aaf2c04ffa0434b6723ffd86ad19376e2ce8.
lessons: A scalar masked identity proxy cannot stand in for visible robot topology.
Topology must be a hard conjunction over full-frame evidence so an average score cannot hide a bad shoulder or duplicate limb.
limitations: The labels are semantic 2-D visual review, not 3-D kinematic reconstruction.
This audit rejects the old output but does not itself repair the generator.
next_actions: Train the first bounded native H3 Ref2VA LoRA round on topology-positive clips and test the same held-out real flower action.
